sentences.text: The estimated body mass of this dinosaur is 11.28 kilograms.
It possessed a functionally monodactyl foot where the large third digit bore most of the weight while walking.
The radius of the arm is 47% the length of the humerus and ten times longer than wide, making it much thinner than most relatives.
The forearm axis is twisted 25 degrees relative to the longitudinal axis.
In the second finger, the penultimate phalanx is not extended, a feature exclusive to Averostra.
The claw of the third finger is short, blunt, and not curved.
The second metatarsal bone is extremely flattened transversely, being less than one-fifth the width of the third metatarsal bone.
The fourth metatarsal bone is strongly flattened, four times narrower than it is wide from front to back.
The phalanx formula for the foot is the usual 2-3-4-5-0 found in related species.
The first phalanx of the first toe is elongated, four times longer than it is wide.
At just 11.28 kilograms, Vespersaurus was an exceptionally light predator.

The genus Vespersaurus was named and described in 2019.
The holotype specimen MPCO.V 0065d was found in dark red sandstones of the Rio Paraná Formation in Brazil.
The fossil site also yielded remains of the small relative Berthasaura, whose toothless beak indicates a herbivorous lifestyle.
Finite Element Analysis showed Vespersaurus teeth were not well suited for struggling or hard prey, with an ideal bite angle of 45 degrees.
Researchers concluded Vespersaurus was a generalist feeder focusing on small prey rather than a top predator.
The second and fourth toes were so flattened transversely that the third toe likely supported most of the animal's weight.
The foot claws were not particularly curved and likely inflicted longitudinal wounds rather than piercing skin.
Researchers suggest the second and fourth claws may have lifted slightly during walking to avoid hindering the push of the long third toe.
Footprints found near the site resemble those of the ichnogenus Sarmientichnus, which some Chinese researchers believe belongs to the Deinonychosauria.
The footprints indicate an animal with a hip height of half a meter that moved quickly with hind legs at right angles.
The genus Vespersaurus was established by Langer et al. in 2019.
Vespersaurus belongs to the family Noasauridae.
Vespersaurus is classified within the subfamily Noasaurinae.

Vespersaurus is classified as a reptile.
The type species of the genus Vespersaurus is Vespersaurus paranaensis.
Vespersaurus is a noasaurid theropod dinosaur from the Cretaceous Rio Paraná Formation in the Paraná Basin, Brazil.
Vespersaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 90 million years ago in the Turonian stage, in what is now South America.
A whole branch of these animals likely populated the 1.3 million square kilometer Botucatu Desert for millions of years.
Vespersaurus lived from the Aptian to the Campanian stages, between 121.4 and 72.2 million years ago.
It is debated whether the ichnospecies Farlowichnus rapidus was made by Vespersaurus, as some researchers question the noasaurid interpretation due to anatomical differences.
